pr.title: Anonymous: Add configurable device limit

raw_findings.body: Wire cannot resolve the new `int64` parameter, so wire generation fails (or the committed wire_gen.go still calls the old one-argument form and the package no longer compiles), breaking the build.
raw_findings.impact: Wire cannot resolve the new `int64` parameter, so wire generation fails (or the committed wire_gen.go still calls the old one-argument form and the package no longer compiles), breaking the build.
raw_findings.root_cause: A wire-managed constructor gained a primitive parameter that has no provider in the wire set, and the wire set/generated code was not updated in the same change.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either keep `ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore db.DB)` and set the limit from cfg inside a wrapper provider, or update pkg/server/wire.go to supply the limit (e.g. a provider returning the value from *setting.Cfg) and regenerate wire_gen.go in the same patch.
raw_findings.title: Provider signature change breaks wire dependency injection
raw_findings.trigger: Building the server / regenerating wire: pkg/server/wire.go still lists `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` in wireBasicSet, and the patch does not add any provider for a bare `int64`.

raw_findings.body: The first request is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached, but `tagDeviceUI` already stored the cache key before calling the store, so the second request short-circuits on the cache, returns nil, and the anonymous user is authenticated without ever being recorded — the device limit is silently bypassed and enforcement is non-deterministic.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Device limit is enforced only for the first request per device per cache TTL, allowing untracked anonymous sessions.
raw_findings.impact: The first request is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached, but `tagDeviceUI` already stored the cache key before calling the store, so the second request short-circuits on the cache, returns nil, and the anonymous user is authenticated without ever being recorded — the device limit is silently bypassed and enforcement is non-deterministic.
raw_findings.root_cause: Propagating the store error out of TagDevice turned a previously best-effort background tagging path into an authorization decision, while the pre-existing cache-before-write ordering leaves the failed device marked as already tagged.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: In `tagDeviceUI`, delete the cache entry (`a.localCache.Delete(key)`) when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns an error, or set the cache entry only after a successful store write.
raw_findings.title: Local cache is populated before store write, so a rejected device is allowed on retry
raw_findings.trigger: device_limit is configured and reached; a new anonymous device sends two requests within the 29 minute localCache TTL.

raw_findings.body: Each request independently reads a count below the limit and then inserts, so the number of tracked anonymous devices exceeds the configured device_limit, defeating the licensing/limit guarantee the feature is meant to provide.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Race window between CountDevices and the INSERT permits over-provisioning of devices.
raw_findings.impact: Each request independently reads a count below the limit and then inserts, so the number of tracked anonymous devices exceeds the configured device_limit, defeating the licensing/limit guarantee the feature is meant to provide.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new limit enforcement uses a separate read query followed by an unguarded write instead of an atomic database operation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Perform the count and the insert inside a single transaction with appropriate locking, or make the insert conditional in SQL (e.g. `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit`) and treat zero inserted rows as ErrDeviceLimitReached.
raw_findings.title: Count-then-insert device limit check is not atomic
raw_findings.trigger: Two or more concurrent anonymous requests with distinct device IDs arrive while the stored device count is exactly `deviceLimit - 1` (or several Grafana instances share the same database).

raw_findings.body: `updateDevice` returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for a device that already exists and is within the limit; client.go then aborts anonymous authentication, denying access to a legitimately tracked device.
raw_findings.failure_mode: False-positive limit error rejects valid anonymous devices on MySQL.
raw_findings.impact: `updateDevice` returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for a device that already exists and is within the limit; client.go then aborts anonymous authentication, denying access to a legitimately tracked device.
raw_findings.root_cause: Using driver-dependent RowsAffected as a proxy for row existence in the new updateDevice path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Determine existence explicitly (e.g. SELECT the device id inside the same transaction, or check `Get` on the row) and only return ErrDeviceLimitReached when no matching non-expired device row exists, rather than inferring it from RowsAffected == 0.
raw_findings.title: Zero rows affected is misinterpreted as device limit reached
raw_findings.trigger: Running on MySQL (where anon_device.updated_at has second precision and RowsAffected reports changed, not matched, rows) with the limit reached: an existing device is updated twice within the same second, so the UPDATE changes nothing.

raw_findings.body: The newly readable `device_limit` key is undiscoverable and its default/semantics (0 = unlimited) are undocumented, so users cannot configure the feature and the shipped config files become stale relative to the code.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Documentation and shipped config drift from the implemented configuration surface.
raw_findings.impact: The newly readable `device_limit` key is undiscoverable and its default/semantics (0 = unlimited) are undocumented, so users cannot configure the feature and the shipped config files become stale relative to the code.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new ini configuration key was added to the settings reader without the accompanying entries in the shipped configuration files/docs.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a commented `device_limit` entry with the default value and a short description to conf/defaults.ini and conf/sample.ini under `[auth.anonymous]`, and document it in the anonymous auth configuration docs.
raw_findings.title: New device_limit option is not documented in defaults.ini/sample.ini
raw_findings.trigger: An operator looks for the new setting in conf/defaults.ini or conf/sample.ini under `[auth.anonymous]` (which currently list only enabled, org_name, org_role, hide_version) or in the anonymous auth docs.

raw_findings.body: The class property type narrows to `undefined` even though the backend always serializes a number into bootData, so numeric usage fails type checking (or silently invites `any`), making the newly exposed setting unusable from the frontend.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Type inference produces a useless field type, breaking or misleading consumers.
raw_findings.impact: The class property type narrows to `undefined` even though the backend always serializes a number into bootData, so numeric usage fails type checking (or silently invites `any`), making the newly exposed setting unusable from the frontend.
raw_findings.root_cause: New class field added with a bare `undefined` initializer and no type annotation, unlike the annotated optional fields around it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Annotate the field explicitly: `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;` (or `anonymousDeviceLimit = 0;`) to match the `GrafanaConfig` declaration.
raw_findings.title: GrafanaBootConfig field is typed as `undefined` instead of `number | undefined`
raw_findings.trigger: Any TypeScript consumer reading `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` and comparing it with a number, given strict compiler settings where the initializer `undefined` infers the field type as `undefined`.

raw_findings.body: Anonymous authentication now blocks on database round-trips (count + upsert) instead of the previous fire-and-forget goroutine with its own 2 minute timeout and panic recovery, so DB latency or contention directly increases request latency and a panic in the tagging path is no longer recovered.
raw_findings.evidence: if err := a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, anonymous.AnonDeviceUI); err != nil {
raw_findings.failure_mode: Request-path latency and fault amplification for every anonymous request.
raw_findings.impact: Anonymous authentication now blocks on database round-trips (count + upsert) instead of the previous fire-and-forget goroutine with its own 2 minute timeout and panic recovery, so DB latency or contention directly increases request latency and a panic in the tagging path is no longer recovered.
raw_findings.root_cause: The asynchronous goroutine (with timeout and recover) was replaced by a direct synchronous call in order to surface the limit error.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the enforcement check synchronous but minimal (e.g. a single conditional insert), or retain a bounded timeout for the tagging call and recover panics so slow/failing storage cannot stall or crash anonymous request handling.
raw_findings.title: Device tagging moved onto the synchronous authentication path
raw_findings.trigger: Any anonymous request whose device cache entry has expired, especially with device_limit > 0 where TagDevice additionally issues a `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM anon_device` before the upsert.

raw_findings.body: The unclassified error propagates through the authn broker and is rendered as a generic internal error instead of a meaningful, translatable client-facing message, giving users no indication that the anonymous device limit was exceeded.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Opaque HTTP error response for a expected, user-facing condition.
raw_findings.impact: The unclassified error propagates through the authn broker and is rendered as a generic internal error instead of a meaningful, translatable client-facing message, giving users no indication that the anonymous device limit was exceeded.
raw_findings.root_cause: New sentinel error created with fmt.Errorf and returned directly from an authn client instead of using the project's errutil-based error contract.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Define ErrDeviceLimitReached with errutil (e.g. errutil.Unauthorized/TooManyRequests with a public message) or wrap it in an `authn.Error` before returning it from Authenticate.
raw_findings.title: Device limit error surfaced to HTTP layer without an errutil status
raw_findings.trigger: An anonymous user hits Grafana after the configured device limit is reached, so Authenticate returns the plain `fmt.Errorf("device limit reached")`.

raw_findings.body: The limit query window, the device listing window and the usage-stats window can silently diverge, producing inconsistent counts between the API, usage stats and limit enforcement.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Maintenance hazard: partial updates lead to inconsistent device windows.
raw_findings.impact: The limit query window, the device listing window and the usage-stats window can silently diverge, producing inconsistent counts between the API, usage stats and limit enforcement.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch introduced a second/third copy of the same duration literal rather than sharing one definition.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Export a single constant (e.g. `anonstore.DeviceExpiration`) and reference it from api/api.go and impl.go instead of redeclaring the literal, replacing the remaining `thirtyDays` constant.
raw_findings.title: Thirty-day expiration constant now duplicated in three packages
raw_findings.trigger: Changing the anonymous device retention window later: the same 30-day value now exists as `anonymousDeviceExpiration` in anonstore, `anonymousDeviceExpiration` in anonimpl/api, and the untouched `thirtyDays` in anonimpl/impl.go.

raw_findings.body: Inconsistent alias usage within the same file (and against the repo's `any` convention), which linters/reviewers flag and which makes the two argument-building blocks look unrelated.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Style inconsistency in newly added code.
raw_findings.impact: Inconsistent alias usage within the same file (and against the repo's `any` convention), which linters/reviewers flag and which makes the two argument-building blocks look unrelated.
raw_findings.root_cause: New helper written with the pre-Go1.18 spelling of the empty interface while the file already standardized on `any`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace `[]interface{}` with `[]any` in both statements of `updateDevice` to match the surrounding code.
raw_findings.title: New code uses []interface{} while adjacent code uses []any
raw_findings.trigger: Reviewing/maintaining database.go, where the sibling `CreateOrUpdateDevice` builds `args := []any{...}` and `append([]any{query}, args...)`.

raw_findings.body: The main intended behaviour of the feature — that an already-known device can still be refreshed (client_ip/user_agent/updated_at updated) while the limit is reached, and that no extra row is inserted — is untested, so a regression in `updateDevice`'s WHERE window or in the count check would not be caught.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test suite passes while the update-under-limit path is unverified.
raw_findings.impact: The main intended behaviour of the feature — that an already-known device can still be refreshed (client_ip/user_agent/updated_at updated) while the limit is reached, and that no extra row is inserted — is untested, so a regression in `updateDevice`'s WHERE window or in the count check would not be caught.
raw_findings.root_cause: New limit-enforcement branch added with coverage only for the rejection path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Extend the test to re-tag the existing device id after the limit is reached, assert NoError and that ListDevices still returns exactly one device with the updated client_ip/user_agent, and add a case where the existing device's updated_at is older than anonymousDeviceExpiration.
raw_findings.title: Device limit test omits the successful-update and no-new-row assertions
raw_findings.trigger: Running TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit: it only asserts that a brand-new device is rejected once the limit is reached.

validated_findings.root_cause: A wire-managed constructor gained a primitive parameter that has no provider in the wire set, and the wire set/generated code was not updated in the same change.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Either keep `ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore db.DB)` and set the limit from cfg inside a wrapper provider, or update pkg/server/wire.go to supply the limit (e.g. a provider returning the value from *setting.Cfg) and regenerate wire_gen.go in the same patch.
validated_findings.title: Provider signature change breaks wire dependency injection
validated_findings.trigger: Building the server / regenerating wire: pkg/server/wire.go still lists `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` in wireBasicSet, and the patch does not add any provider for a bare `int64`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch shows ProvideAnonDBStore is called directly in impl.go:43 with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit, bypassing wire injection. The wire.go binding at line 374 still lists anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore but ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer takes anonStore as parameter - it constructs it internally. Wire won't fail because the provider is not used for injection into ProvideAnonymousDeviceService anymore.

validated_findings.body: The first request is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached, but `tagDeviceUI` already stored the cache key before calling the store, so the second request short-circuits on the cache, returns nil, and the anonymous user is authenticated without ever being recorded — the device limit is silently bypassed and enforcement is non-deterministic.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Device limit is enforced only for the first request per device per cache TTL, allowing untracked anonymous sessions.
validated_findings.impact: The first request is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached, but `tagDeviceUI` already stored the cache key before calling the store, so the second request short-circuits on the cache, returns nil, and the anonymous user is authenticated without ever being recorded — the device limit is silently bypassed and enforcement is non-deterministic.
validated_findings.root_cause: Propagating the store error out of TagDevice turned a previously best-effort background tagging path into an authorization decision, while the pre-existing cache-before-write ordering leaves the failed device marked as already tagged.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: In `tagDeviceUI`, delete the cache entry (`a.localCache.Delete(key)`) when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns an error, or set the cache entry only after a successful store write.
validated_findings.title: Local cache is populated before store write, so a rejected device is allowed on retry
validated_findings.trigger: device_limit is configured and reached; a new anonymous device sends two requests within the 29 minute localCache TTL.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at impl.go:87 shows localCache.SetDefault is called before CreateOrUpdateDevice at line 93. If CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry remains, so subsequent requests within TTL will short-circuit at line 83-84 and return nil, bypassing the limit check.

validated_findings.body: Each request independently reads a count below the limit and then inserts, so the number of tracked anonymous devices exceeds the configured device_limit, defeating the licensing/limit guarantee the feature is meant to provide.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Race window between CountDevices and the INSERT permits over-provisioning of devices.
validated_findings.impact: Each request independently reads a count below the limit and then inserts, so the number of tracked anonymous devices exceeds the configured device_limit, defeating the licensing/limit guarantee the feature is meant to provide.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new limit enforcement uses a separate read query followed by an unguarded write instead of an atomic database operation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Perform the count and the insert inside a single transaction with appropriate locking, or make the insert conditional in SQL (e.g. `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit`) and treat zero inserted rows as ErrDeviceLimitReached.
validated_findings.title: Count-then-insert device limit check is not atomic
validated_findings.trigger: Two or more concurrent anonymous requests with distinct device IDs arrive while the stored device count is exactly `deviceLimit - 1` (or several Grafana instances share the same database).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at database.go:109-117 shows CountDevices is called, then if count < deviceLimit the insert proceeds. No transaction or lock protects this sequence, allowing concurrent requests to each read count below limit and then insert, exceeding the configured limit.

validated_findings.body: `updateDevice` returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for a device that already exists and is within the limit; client.go then aborts anonymous authentication, denying access to a legitimately tracked device.
validated_findings.failure_mode: False-positive limit error rejects valid anonymous devices on MySQL.
validated_findings.impact: `updateDevice` returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for a device that already exists and is within the limit; client.go then aborts anonymous authentication, denying access to a legitimately tracked device.
validated_findings.root_cause: Using driver-dependent RowsAffected as a proxy for row existence in the new updateDevice path.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Determine existence explicitly (e.g. SELECT the device id inside the same transaction, or check `Get` on the row) and only return ErrDeviceLimitReached when no matching non-expired device row exists, rather than inferring it from RowsAffected == 0.
validated_findings.title: Zero rows affected is misinterpreted as device limit reached
validated_findings.trigger: Running on MySQL (where anon_device.updated_at has second precision and RowsAffected reports changed, not matched, rows) with the limit reached: an existing device is updated twice within the same second, so the UPDATE changes nothing.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at database.go:95-96 shows rowsAffected==0 returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL, UPDATE returns rows changed not matched, so updating a device with identical values (same second precision) yields 0 affected rows, incorrectly triggering the limit error for an existing valid device.

validated_findings.body: The newly readable `device_limit` key is undiscoverable and its default/semantics (0 = unlimited) are undocumented, so users cannot configure the feature and the shipped config files become stale relative to the code.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Documentation and shipped config drift from the implemented configuration surface.
validated_findings.impact: The newly readable `device_limit` key is undiscoverable and its default/semantics (0 = unlimited) are undocumented, so users cannot configure the feature and the shipped config files become stale relative to the code.
validated_findings.root_cause: A new ini configuration key was added to the settings reader without the accompanying entries in the shipped configuration files/docs.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a commented `device_limit` entry with the default value and a short description to conf/defaults.ini and conf/sample.ini under `[auth.anonymous]`, and document it in the anonymous auth configuration docs.
validated_findings.title: New device_limit option is not documented in defaults.ini/sample.ini
validated_findings.trigger: An operator looks for the new setting in conf/defaults.ini or conf/sample.ini under `[auth.anonymous]` (which currently list only enabled, org_name, org_role, hide_version) or in the anonymous auth docs.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch adds device_limit at setting.go:1654 but the repository context shows conf/defaults.ini and conf/sample.ini under [auth.anonymous] only list enabled, org_name, org_role, hide_version - no device_limit entry. The new config key is undocumented.

validated_findings.body: The class property type narrows to `undefined` even though the backend always serializes a number into bootData, so numeric usage fails type checking (or silently invites `any`), making the newly exposed setting unusable from the frontend.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Type inference produces a useless field type, breaking or misleading consumers.
validated_findings.impact: The class property type narrows to `undefined` even though the backend always serializes a number into bootData, so numeric usage fails type checking (or silently invites `any`), making the newly exposed setting unusable from the frontend.
validated_findings.root_cause: New class field added with a bare `undefined` initializer and no type annotation, unlike the annotated optional fields around it.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Annotate the field explicitly: `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;` (or `anonymousDeviceLimit = 0;`) to match the `GrafanaConfig` declaration.
validated_findings.title: GrafanaBootConfig field is typed as `undefined` instead of `number | undefined`
validated_findings.trigger: Any TypeScript consumer reading `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` and comparing it with a number, given strict compiler settings where the initializer `undefined` infers the field type as `undefined`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at config.ts:97 shows 'anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;' with no type annotation. TypeScript infers the type as 'undefined' rather than 'number | undefined' as declared in grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200, causing type mismatch.

validated_findings.body: Anonymous authentication now blocks on database round-trips (count + upsert) instead of the previous fire-and-forget goroutine with its own 2 minute timeout and panic recovery, so DB latency or contention directly increases request latency and a panic in the tagging path is no longer recovered.
validated_findings.evidence: if err := a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, anonymous.AnonDeviceUI); err != nil {
validated_findings.failure_mode: Request-path latency and fault amplification for every anonymous request.
validated_findings.impact: Anonymous authentication now blocks on database round-trips (count + upsert) instead of the previous fire-and-forget goroutine with its own 2 minute timeout and panic recovery, so DB latency or contention directly increases request latency and a panic in the tagging path is no longer recovered.
validated_findings.root_cause: The asynchronous goroutine (with timeout and recover) was replaced by a direct synchronous call in order to surface the limit error.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the enforcement check synchronous but minimal (e.g. a single conditional insert), or retain a bounded timeout for the tagging call and recover panics so slow/failing storage cannot stall or crash anonymous request handling.
validated_findings.title: Device tagging moved onto the synchronous authentication path
validated_findings.trigger: Any anonymous request whose device cache entry has expired, especially with device_limit > 0 where TagDevice additionally issues a `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM anon_device` before the upsert.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at client.go:44-50 shows TagDevice is now called synchronously (removed goroutine with timeout and recover from lines 45-57 in LEFT). DB operations now block the authentication path and panics are no longer recovered.
